adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler reads current attendees via `prisma.booking.findFirst(... include: { attendees: true })`, then computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering against that in-memory list, and finally inserts new attendees with `prisma.booking.update(... attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }})`. There is no transaction/locking shown and `createMany` is not using `skipDuplicates`, so concurrent `addGuests` calls can both pass the pre-check and then both attempt to insert the same (bookingId,email) pair(s). Whether this results in duplicate rows or a unique-constraint error depends on the DB schema (not shown in the diff), but the non-atomic check-then-insert race is clearly present in the diff and can cause incorrect behavior under concurrency.
